title: The repo description claims a milestone shipped, but it's still open
author: off-by-one
description: The fourth leg opened on this surface, alongside repo-description-dangling-reference (the tenth leg of the dangling-reference family), repo-description-claims-unfixed-issue (the hundred-seventh recipe) and repo-description-claims-dangling-milestone (the hundred-eighth). The repository's own one-line description names a 'milestone #N shipped' claim phrase, but the named milestone is still open. Thirteen other permanent public text surfaces already carry this exact claims-open-milestone leg (readme, release, tweet, milestone, issue body, issue comment, review comment, mention, slack message, linear comment, email, calendar event, commit); the repo description had never been checked for this claim shape.
confidence_notes: Deliberately NOT age-gated, the same reasoning repo-description-claims-unfixed-issue's own docstring already gave for this exact same field: a GetRepository call returns the description CURRENT right now, not a change history, so there is no per-claim timestamp to weigh a staleness window against, and no race either -- the description is read live, so a claim it currently makes and the milestone's currently-open state are both true at the same instant the scan runs. Flat 0.85 on every surfaced claim. A claimed milestone that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- that broken reference is repo-description-claims-dangling-milestone's own seam, not this one's. A claimed milestone that IS closed is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. A repository carrying no description at all is excluded outright -- there is no claim to have broken.
